note: Adapted from the genus-level account in Roonwal & Chhotani (1989) (in English), whose description is adapted from the original description of Roonwal & Sen-Sarma 1960; the alate, soldier and pseudoworker are all described and measured, and the type specimen was examined (Type examined).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule pale chestnut-brown; pronotum and dorsum of the abdomen slightly paler than the head; antennae, labrum, legs and sternites pale yellow. Head and body hairs medium. Body length with wings 16.3 mm, without wings 7.0—9.0 mm. Head capsule almost square, the sides slightly converging and rounded behind the compound eyes; head width including the compound eyes about equal to the head length to the base of the mandibles (length 1.9 mm, width 1.9 mm); Y suture prominent. Compound eyes large and nearly circular, diameter 0.60—0.65 mm, close against the antennae, the eye-to-antenna distance 0.023—0.038 mm. Ocelli oval and translucent, slightly separated from the compound eyes but almost touching (long diameter 0.23 mm, eye-to-ocellus distance 0.0125 mm). Antennae more than 16-segmented; segment 2 longer than segment 3; segments 3 and 4 about equal, from segment 5 onwards gradually longer. Postclypeus almost rectangular, darker than the frons, with one hair on either side of the middle of the anterior margin; anteclypeus trapezoidal, hairless but with a hair covering. Labrum almost square, the sides rounded and the anterior margin nearly straight, length 0.50 mm, width 0.60 mm, hairy in front and on the surface. Pronotum almost rectangular, slightly wider than the head and about twice as wide as long (length 1.10 mm, width 2.2 mm); anterior margin weakly incurved, sides rounded, posterior margin nearly straight; neither anterior nor posterior margin with a median notch; margins and surface with long and short hairs. Legs slender and hairy, apical tibial spur formula 3:3:3, tarsi 4-segmented, arolia pale yellow. Wings transparent, without nodules and hairless. Fore wing length 14.90 mm: the subcosta meets the costa at a quarter of the wing, the radius meets the subcosta-costa almost at the middle of the wing, the radius sector has 5—7 branches, the media has about 12 cross-veins to the radius sector, the media and cubitus are reticulate between them, and the cubitus has 10 branches. Hind wing length 13.0 mm: the radius meets the subcosta-costa slightly beyond the middle of the wing, the radius sector has 6 branches, the media arises from the radius sector at the proximal fifth of the wing, and the cubitus has 14 branches. Abdomen slender and hairy; cerci 2-segmented.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule pale brown to brown; antennae brownish at the base and paler at the tip; mandibles almost black, the base dark brown with a reddish tinge; legs and body yellow-white. Head and body sparsely hairy. Body length 10.5—13.2 mm. Head capsule almost rectangular, widest at the base of the antennae and slightly converging behind (length to the base of the mandibles 3.69—4.30 mm, width 2.40—2.52 mm); frons sloping at about 45° in front, with a median depression extending backwards to the middle of the dorsum of the head; Y suture not visible. Compound eyes whitish and translucent, oval, length 0.30—0.33 mm, about one eye length from the antennae. Ocelli absent. Antennae 14—15-segmented; antennal carinae weak; segment 3 about as long as segment 2; segment 4 shorter, the following segments gradually longer, the terminal segment slightly shorter than the penultimate. Postclypeus almost rectangular, with 2 pairs of hairs on the anterior margin; anteclypeus almost trapezoidal, whitish and hairless; labrum small and almost rectangular, the anterior margin rounded (length 0.54 mm, width 0.66—0.78 mm), hairy near the anterior margin. Mandibles short and stout, about half the head length (length 1.9—2.07 mm, mandible length/head length index 0.48—0.53); outer margin strongly raised at the base. Left mandible with 5 and right mandible with 2 large marginal teeth, situated in the basal half. Postmentum long and clavate; the club strongly bilobed; the stalk long and the waist narrow; medium length 2.90—3.06 mm, greatest width 0.9 mm, waist width 0.3—0.42 mm. Pronotum almost rectangular, longer than half its width, about as wide as or slightly wider than the head (length 1.3—1.53 mm, width 2.5—2.79 mm); anterolateral angles acutely rounded; sides weakly convex and slightly converging backwards; anterior margin strongly incurved without a notch; posterior margin nearly straight. Legs short and slender; apical tibial spur formula 3:3:3, tarsi 4-segmented. Abdomen slender and hairy, each tergite with a row of hairs; cerci 2-segmented and short.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Pseudoworker: head pale straw; labrum, antennae and body creamy white. Head and body hairs medium. Body length 8.5 mm. Head almost square (length to the base of the mandibles 1.9 mm, width 2.0 mm). Compound eyes reduced, small and whitish, visible only in strong light. Antennae 15-segmented; segment 3 shorter than segment 2; segments 3, 4 and 5 about equal and the shortest. Postclypeus almost rectangular, darker than the head, with 2 pairs of hairs on the anterior margin; anteclypeus trapezoidal and hairless. Labrum almost rectangular, the anterior margin nearly straight, hairy on the anterior margin and surface. Mandibles as in the genus. Pronotum almost rectangular, wider than the head (length 1.2 mm, width 2.4 mm); anterior margin concave, posterior margin nearly straight. Legs and abdomen as in the soldier.
